patent_grounding.rationale: Revision 4’s new DIVE–BODY suspension-linkage connection is supported by claim 7’s express connection of the suspension linkage to both ends of the frame upright, read with claim 4’s body-side linkage attachment. The selected roll bell-crank embodiment, wheel/ski attachment, and locking behavior are also supported by the cited passages. The alternative hydraulic embodiment remains excluded.

functional_completeness.rationale: The prior missing DIVE-to-BODY/frame-upright attachment is now explicitly modeled with a distinct interface, in addition to the roll-to-dive push-rod connection and wheel/ski attachment. Major relationships in the selected claimed topology and behavior are represented; alternative configurations are explicitly out of scope.

flow_consistency.rationale: The new linkage interface connects existing DIVE_BODY_LINK and BODY_DIVE_LINK ports, both mechanical_motion and bidirectional, and references the existing F_DIVE_BODY_LINK flow. It is distinct from the ROLL–DIVE push-rod flow and from the roll/body pivot coupling. No incompatible transformation is modeled as an interface.

claim_traceability.rationale: The newly added interface and flow cite claim/specification text supporting the frame-upright linkage attachment; its notes identify claims 4 and 7. Actions remain claim-grounded mechanical behavior, not electronic control. No unsupported engineering requirement is introduced.

interfaces.rationale: The revision resolves the prior topology concern. DIVE_BODY_LINK to BODY_DIVE_LINK has compatible ports and a matching item flow; the added connection is separate from the push-rod interface. Other modeled connections also refer to existing endpoints and flows.

textbook_application.rationale: Retrieved guidance supports distinguishing physical subsystems/interfaces and selecting a specific physical decomposition, but does not supply invention facts. It is not used as patent evidence. The model consistently represents one supported embodiment and leaves alternatives outside the model.

summary: Independent review of saved revision 4: the prior concern is resolved. The new DIVE-to-BODY linkage interface coherently represents the patent-supported suspension linkage connection to both ends of the frame upright, with compatible bidirectional mechanical-motion ports and its own flow, distinct from the roll push rod. The selected bell-crank embodiment and modeled behavior remain grounded in patent passages; no unsupported requirements or new material issues were found. Textbook guidance is applied only to modeling choices, not invention facts. No structural findings were reported in the supplied context.
